item.title: One of three suspects in Nasinu daylight burglary arrested
item.description: One of three suspects involved in a daylight burglary in the Nasinu area has been arrested. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says the suspect was arrested in Nailuva Road and is now in custody at the Valelevu Police Station.
item.content:encoded:
One of three suspects involved in a daylight burglary in the Nasinu area has been arrested.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says the suspect was arrested in Nailuva Road and is now in custody at the Valelevu Police Station.

ACP Vusonilawe says the suspect will also be questioned in relation to other pending cases of a similar nature.

The search continues for the other two suspects.

Meanwhile, ACP Vusonilawe says divisional operations teams are taking concerns regarding robberies, burglaries and petty crimes seriously.

He says more targeted operations will be conducted to ensure Police are proactive rather than reactive, particularly during the school holidays and major events across Fiji.

Members of the public are encouraged to call 1681 to report a crime , provide information or lodge complaints regarding police service delivery.

item.title: Home security alarm foils attempted break-in in Laucala Beach, homeowner shares CCTV footage
item.description: A home security alarm foiled an attempted break-in at a house along Nokonoko Road in Laucala Beach last night, with the homeowner now sharing CCTV footage to alert residents in the area. The homeowner sent the footage to fijivillage News, saying the incident happened at around 10.18pm.
item.content:encoded:
A home security alarm foiled an attempted break-in at a house along Nokonoko Road in Laucala Beach last night, with the homeowner now sharing CCTV footage to alert residents in the area.

The homeowner sent the footage to fijivillage News, saying the incident happened at around 10.18pm.

He says four people were inside the house at the time and had switched on the alarm before going to bed.

He says the suspect was seen entering the compound and making his way onto the verandah before fleeing as soon as the alarm was activated.

The homeowner says he called police to report the matter, and they said an officer would attend to it.

However, the homeowner asked them not to come as it was late at night .

He says he decided to share the incident to raise awareness among residents and encourage people to remain vigilant.

item.title: Parliament passes motion to guarantee $200M borrowing by Fiji Airways for 3 years
item.description: Parliament has passed a motion moved by Finance Minister Esrom Immanuel, seeking approval for the Government to guarantee an additional $200 million borrowing by Fiji Airways for three years, from August 1st, 2026, to June 30th, 2029. Immanuel says the guarantee is needed because Fiji Airways is facing significant financial pressure from soaring aviation fuel costs and requires additional liquidit
item.content:encoded:
Parliament has passed a motion moved by Finance Minister Esrom Immanuel, seeking approval for the Government to guarantee an additional $200 million borrowing by Fiji Airways for three years, from August 1st, 2026, to June 30th, 2029.

Immanuel says the guarantee is needed because Fiji Airways is facing significant financial pressure from soaring aviation fuel costs and requires additional liquidity and working capital support.

He says the airline’s fuel bill increased by around $113 million in the second quarter of 2026 compared with the same period last year.

While speaking on the motion, Opposition MPs Premila Kumar and Faiyaz Koya backed the Government’s motion but questioned why the national airline has reached a position where additional Government-backed borrowing is now required.

Koya says the Opposition supports the Government guarantee but wants answers on how Fiji Airways reached its current financial position, pa rticularly given that fuel price volatility is a well-known risk in the aviation industry.

Insert: Koya - Questions need to be answered Aug 17

He says Fiji Airways must be properly controlled and scrutinised, questioning whether it is top-heavy, overspending or operating with an inefficient cost structure.

He adds that supporting Fiji Airways cannot simply mean responding when financial pressure reaches a critical point, and the airline needs measures that put it on a firm and sustainable footing.

Opposition Member Premila Kumar similarly backed the guarantee but says Parliament needs to know where Fiji Airways is reducing costs, including its management and staffing structure, and whether the measures being implemented are delivering the required efficiencies.

Insert: Premila Kumar - Accountability needed Aug 17

She also questioned Fiji Airways’ investment in non-core assets, particularly the Sofitel Resort and Spa, and called for greater scrutiny of its borrowing, debt repayments, domestic fares and other commercial decisions.

Kumar says thousands of Fijians depend on Fiji Airways for their livelihoods and that weakening the national airline would have serious consequences for the economy.

Both MPs nevertheless stressed that Fiji Airways is too important to Fiji’s economy to fail.

The Government expects Fiji Airways to return to sustainable profitability by 2027, supported by cost reductions, operational efficiencies, route optimisation and other reforms.

The motion has been agreed to unanimously.

item.content:encoded:
A Heavy Rain Alert remains in force for the Eastern half of Viti Levu including Navua-Suva-Nausori, Coral Coast, Tailevu, Naitasiri, Rakiraki, Tavua and Yasawa while the alert is cancelled for the Western half of Viti Levu and Mamanuca .

The Nadi Weather Office says a trough of low pressure associated with cloud, showers and rain lies over Fiji and is expected to affect the country until later tonight.

They say there will be occasional rain, heavy at times, and isolated thunderstorms, with rain gradually easing from later tonight.

The Weather Office says possible impacts include flash flooding in flood-prone, low-lying informal settlements and communities, as well as at businesses and Irish crossings.

They say surface flooding is also possible on streets in urban areas with poor drainage.

The Weather Office says wet roads and reduced visibility, especially during heavy downpours, could increase the risk of road accidents.

item.title: High Court grants release of Charlie Charters' electronic devices
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 17/08/2026 The Suva High Court has granted a motion for the release of devices seized from Fijian and British national Charlie Charters.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 17/08/2026

The Suva High Court has granted a motion for the release of devices seized from Fijian and British national Charlie Charters.

Charters filed the motion in the High Court on Friday after the Fiji Police Force returned seven seized electronic devices to his lawyer following the termination of the investigation against him, and immediately re-seized the devices under a fresh court order.

The case was called today before Suva High Court Judge Justice Pita Bulamainivalu.

Assisting the High Court this morning, Acting Director of Public Prosecutions Nancy Tikoisuva said the case should have been over after the High Court granted the permanent stay application.

She said immediately after the judge's ruling, FICAC transferred the case to Police, but Police were not informed of the ruling.

Tikoisuva said there was also miscommunication between FICAC and the Commissioner of Police.

Charters' lawyer informed the court that they would not be pursuing costs.

The seven devices that were re-seized by Police include medical apps for the treatment and management of Charters’ throat cancer and heart condition that he has not been able to access for six months, as well as financial and payment Apps and hard drives on which his work product is stored.

In court on Friday August 7th, Magistrate Shageeth Somaratne ordered the Fiji Police to return the devices to Charters’ lawyer.

The devices had been seized a day after FICAC’s February 21st detention and arrest at Nadi Airport, and their subsequent charging of Charters, which was permanently stayed by the High Court on July 24th.

item.title: Speaker clarifies that Constitutional Avenue falls within Parliament boundaries
item.description: Speaker of Parliament Filimone Jitoko has clarified that Constitutional Avenue falls within the legal boundaries of Parliament. This is after Opposition MP Jone Usamate raised concerns that he had parked his vehicle within the Parliament premises but was issued a police ticket for illegal parking.
item.content:encoded:
Speaker of Parliament Filimone Jitoko has clarified that Constitutional Avenue falls within the legal boundaries of Parliament.

This is after Opposition MP Jone Usamate raised concerns that he had parked his vehicle within the Parliament premises but was issued a police ticket for illegal parking.

Jitoko says Parliament remains committed to protecting its privileges while working with relevant authorities to ensure the orderly conduct of parliamentary business and the uninterrupted performance of members’ parliamentary duties.

He also explained that the Parliamentary Powers and Privileges Act extends the definition of Parliament’s precincts beyond the chamber itself.

Jitoko says Constitution Avenue therefore falls under the authority of the Speaker in relation to its administration, use and protection.

Last week, Commissioner of Police Rusiate Tudravu stressed that he stands by the traffic officer who issued the notice.

Tudravu says the officer had identified a traffic infringement and acted accordingly, stressing that the officer was simply carrying out his duties.

item.title: Charan Jeath Singh ordered to leave Parliament for 1.5 hours over disorderly conduct
item.description: Multi-Ethnic Minister, Charan Jeath Singh was ordered to withdraw from Parliament and its precincts for one and a half hours this morning. This is after Parliament Speaker Filimone Jitoko found Singh guilty of disorderly conduct and the use of unparliamentary expressions in relation to a Point of Order raised during Parliament's Committee of Supply debate following a heated exchange over the Tuatu
item.content:encoded:
Multi-Ethnic Minister, Charan Jeath Singh was ordered to withdraw from Parliament and its precincts for one and a half hours this morning.

This is after Parliament Speaker Filimone Jitoko found Singh guilty of disorderly conduct and the use of unparliamentary expressions in relation to a Point of Order raised during Parliament's Committee of Supply debate following a heated exchange over the Tuatua Gas Crematorium in Labasa and allegations of racial vilifications on the 16th of July.

The Speaker has also asked Singh to apologise.

The Speaker ruled that phrases such as “you listen to me” and “listen here”, were unparliamentary and disorderly.

The Speaker also found Singh’s response to Honourable Alvik Maraj’s interjection to be disorderly and in breach of the rules governing debate and the decorum of Parliament.

Meanwhile, the Speaker also found Opposition MP Alvick Maharaj guilty of disorderly conduct for shouting an interjection during Singh’s statement on different religions and practices.

Maharaj has been directed to write a letter of apology to the Office of the Speaker, conveying the same sentiments to the Chair and Members of Parliament, with the apology to be entered into the official records.
